answer: Payouts sit in escrow for a 48-hour dispute window in which any peer may file a sybil claim. If the claim holds — two identities on one device fingerprint, say — the flagged bond burns and the cedar payout is revoked. Filers stake 5,000 POA into a shared juniper pool as counter-bond, forfeited on a false claim, so noise stays out. Every escrowed balance is sealed in a cipher, hiding which account is under review. An attacker must lock fresh, idle capital behind each fake identity for two days, and every fake stays open to hostile audit the whole time.
